subject: ACME MSA + Order Form — AI-output indemnity carveout & redlines
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-02-11T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: ACME MSA + Order Form — AI-output indemnity carveout & redlines

Team —

Acme procurement surfaced the attached MSA + order form and they are insisting on a very broad indemnity tied to any third-party IP claim arising from model outputs. They want us to: defend + indemnify for any allegation of infringement that traces back to an output the model produced, and they are also asking to remove our defense-control language.

High level asks from me: can legal draft a holder position (1) recommended language we can propose today, (2) a fallback compromise we can live with if they push back, and (3) a short internal justification note for sales to use during procurement. Procurement wants this answered before the next commercial call on Friday.

Key constraints to keep in mind:
- We must avoid open-ended exposure for model training data or model architecture (we rely on open data + third-party licensed corpora).
- Customer-provided data (Customer Data) exposure is acceptable to take on where the claim ties directly to that data.
- If we accept any defense obligation, we should keep defense-control or an express right to assume after timely written notice and cure period.

Attached: ACME_MSA_redline_markus_20260211.docx (core redline), OrderForm_redline_kimberly_20260211.pdf (pricing/term notes).

Markus
Head of Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-11T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: ACME MSA + Order Form — AI-output indemnity carveout & redlines

Markus / Priyom —

Quick draft positions after reviewing Acme's initial asks:

1) Preferred position (what we propose to send):
- "Vendor will defend and indemnify Customer against third-party claims alleging direct infringement to the extent the claim arises from (a) Customer Data provided to Vendor and processed by the Services, or (b) output that reproduces third-party copyrighted material verbatim and such reproduction is causally linked to Customer's prompt and inputs."
- Exclude claims that arise solely from Vendor's model training data, model architecture, or general model behavior.
- Require: prompt notice, cooperation, and exclusive remedy/cap (e.g., aggregate cap of the greater of $500k or fees paid in prior 12 months).
- Defense control: Vendor retains primary defense rights; Customer may assume if Vendor fails to timely defend.

2) Fallback compromise (negotiation sweet spot):
- Accept indemnity for (a) Customer Data and (b) outputs shown (via reasonable proof) to be substantially verbatim from a third-party work; add insurance-first / insurer-step-in approach and carve out punitive damages.
- Introduce an "evidence threshold" for claims to qualify (sample outputs, timestamps, and prompt history).

3) Ops/legal checklist for Sales talking points:
- Why we limit to Customer Data / verbatim reproduction: protects us from open-source training corpora risk.
- Insurance + escrow optional: ask for their certificate of insurance and require mitigation cooperation.
- Proposed SLA: 30 days to assume defense; can we require sublimit or escrow only for claims above $200k.

I attached a redline with inline comments (OrderForm has a short note on liability cap we should keep). If we proceed with fallback, I'm comfortable authorizing commercial to accept insurance-first language but not an open defend-and-indemnify for all outputs.

[Attachment: OrderForm_redline_kimberly_20260211.pdf]

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Patel <sara@brightlanelegal.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme.com>, Dan Price <dan.price@acme.com>
Date: 2026-02-12T08:30:00-05:00
Subject: RE: ACME MSA + Order Form — AI-output indemnity carveout & redlines

Markus —

Thanks for the heads up and the redlines. Acme's position is driven by a recent vendor incident; they need vendor certainty that they will be made whole for third-party claims arising from outputs shown to infringe third-party IP, regardless of where the vendor's model got the material.

High-level counterproposal from Acme:
- Vendor will defend and indemnify Customer for third-party claims arising from any model output delivered to Customer that, when compared to the asserted third-party work, is substantially similar and/or reproduces protected elements.
- Customer must be able to step in and control the defense if Vendor declines or fails to provide adequate defense; we are not comfortable with an absolute vendor defense-control.
- We are open to a mitigation framework: insurance-first (vendor must carry minimum PI/IP insurance of $5M) and an escrowed holdback for low-frequency/high-severity claims.

We included a marked-up MSA with alternative language. We are willing to accept limited proof obligations (samples, prompt logs) but cannot accept language that broadly exempts the vendor for all training-data-derived risk — Acme's legal team says that would leave them exposed.

I've attached our markup — happy to jump on a call to work through one paragraph at a time.

Best,
Sara Patel
Brightlane Legal (external counsel to Acme)
[Attachment: Acme_proposed_msa_markup_brightlane_20260212.docx]

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-12T09:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: ACME MSA + Order Form — AI-output indemnity carveout & redlines

Markus / Kim —

Thanks, Sara — noted. Internal summary / proposed negotiation script for Sales (short):

1) Our ask to Acme: limit vendor indemnity to (i) Customer Data, and (ii) demonstrable verbatim reproduction of a third-party work (we will require sample output + prompt logs). We will not accept indemnity for general model behavior or for allegations tied to our training corpus.

2) Concessions we can make quickly:
- Agree to an insurance-first approach: confirm vendor PI/IP insurance at $5M and require certificate before signing.
- Add a workable defense control compromise: vendor retains primary control but Customer can assume after 30 days if vendor fails; in such an event, costs incurred in assumption count against the cap.
- Add an evidence and notice flow: preserved prompt logs + output snapshots within 30 days of notice; failure to preserve reduces indemnity.

3) Operational ask for Sales/Ops: we need to be able to export prompt + output timestamps for any customer who signs the higher indemnity commitment; please confirm with engineering if log retention at 90 days is feasible.

If Acme pushes for a blanket defense without our carveouts, recommend we offer the fallback: indemnity for Customer Data + verbatim reproduction + escrow sublimit $200k, insurer-step-in for larger claims. Kimberly: if that language looks ok, I recommend we accept the insurance-first + escrow compromise to keep the deal moving.

Subject: Re: ACME MSA + Order Form — AI-output indemnity carveout & redlines

All —

Thanks for the quick turn. I approve the fallback path that Priyom laid out:
- Limited indemnity for Customer Data and demonstrable verbatim reproduction only;
- Insurance-first requirement ($5M PI/IP) plus escrow sublimit $200k for first-instance claims;
- Vendor retains primary defense control but customer able to assume after 30 days; evidence-preservation requirement (prompt logs + outputs).

Kimberly, please prepare a clean counter with that language and include the certificate-of-insurance clause + DocuSign-ready signature block. Priyom / Sales: confirm engineering can retain prompt/output logs for 90 days — if not, we will need to negotiate a shorter window.

I'll send the counter this afternoon to Brightlane/Acme with a short negotiation timeline (48 hours for a commercial reply).

Markus
